title: Your emergency fund: the first money goal

sections.body: An emergency fund is cash set aside only for real surprises: a job loss, a car repair, a medical bill. It keeps one bad month from turning into credit card debt.
A common target is 3 to 6 months of essential expenses: rent or mortgage, food, utilities, insurance, transport and minimum debt payments.

items: Start small. A first goal of $500 to $1,000 already covers many surprise bills.
Keep it separate from your spending account so it doesn't get used by accident.
Keep it easy to reach and safe, like a high-yield savings account, not in stocks.
Aim for the higher end if your income is irregular or you're the only earner.

sections.body: Once your emergency fund is in place, you can focus extra money on paying off high-interest debt and investing.

quiz.q: What is a common emergency fund target?
quiz.why: 3 to 6 months of essentials covers most job searches and big surprise bills.

quiz.q: Where is a good place to keep an emergency fund?
options: In a separate, easy-access savings account
quiz.why: It should be safe and quick to reach. Stocks can drop right when you need the money.

quiz.q: Which of these is a real emergency?
options: A sale on a new phone
A car repair you need to get to work
quiz.why: Emergency money is for necessary, unexpected costs, not planned wants.

disclaimer: Educational content only, not financial advice.
